title: Untensored base change for an arbitrary scheme over the field
statement:
Let $K$ be a field. Let $Z$ and $S'$ be $K$-schemes and let $g:T\to S'$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism. Put $X'=Z\times_{\operatorname{Spec}K}S'$ and $Y=X'\times_{S'}T$, with projections $p:X'\to Z$, $f':X'\to S'$, $h:Y\to X'$ and $e:Y\to T$. Let $\ell$ be a prime invertible in $K$. For every sheaf $\mathcal F$ of $\mathbf F_\ell$-vector spaces on $T_{\mathrm{et}}$, the canonical map
$$(f')^{-1}Rg_*\mathcal F\longrightarrow Rh_*e^{-1}\mathcal F$$
is an isomorphism in $D^+(X'_{\mathrm{et}},\mathbf F_\ell)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. The map is the $h^{-1}\dashv Rh_*$-adjoint of $e^{-1}g^{-1}Rg_*\mathcal F\xrightarrow{e^{-1}\varepsilon_g}e^{-1}\mathcal F$, using $h^{-1}(f')^{-1}=e^{-1}g^{-1}$ and the inverse-image/direct-image adjunction of [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. No finite-type hypothesis on $Z$, $S'$ or $T$ is imposed.

source.place: Tags 0F1I and 0EZT, arbitrary-scheme extension in the proof of Tag 0F1J

proof.text: Put $A=\operatorname{For}(\mathcal F)$, its underlying abelian sheaf. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exchange-forget-coefficients] with coefficient ring $\mathbf F_\ell$, direct-image morphisms $g,h$, and inverse-image morphisms $f',e$. Its clauses (1)--(3) identify the forgotten map in the statement with the bounded-below abelian exchange $\beta_A:(f')^{-1}Rg_*A\to Rh_*e^{-1}A$, and its final assertion says that invertibility is equivalent. Each stalk of $A$ is killed by $\ell$: every element has order $1$ or $\ell$, both invertible in $K$. We prove invertibility of this abelian exchange in the following steps.

source.place: Tag 0F1I, lemma-punctual-base-change, first paragraph of proof; Tag 0EZT, lemma-base-change-Rf-star-colim, assertion (2)

proof.text: The assertion is local on $Z$. Indeed, for an affine open $U\subset Z$ put $X'_U=U\times_KS'$ and $Y_U=U\times_KT$, with open inclusions $j:X'_U\to X'$ and $j_Y:Y_U\to Y$. For a bounded-below injective resolution $I$ of $e^{-1}A$, the resolution formula in [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] computes $Rh_*e^{-1}A$ as $h_*I$. By [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-exact] and [lem-weil-pbc-etale-restriction-injectives], $j_Y^{-1}I$ is an injective resolution of the restricted coefficient. The termwise underived exchange is an isomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-underived-exchange-restriction], since $j$ is an open immersion, hence etale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale]. As $j_Y^{-1}I$ is a bounded below complex of injectives, it is K-injective by [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-derived-exchange-termwise] to the square $(h,h_U,j,j_Y)$, the object $e^{-1}A$ and its resolution $I$, taking $j_Y^{-1}I$ itself, with the identity, as the K-injective resolution of $j_Y^{-1}I$: up to the isomorphisms of its endpoints given there, the derived exchange is $Q$ of the termwise underived exchange, an isomorphism of complexes. Thus the derived exchange $j^{-1}Rh_*e^{-1}A\to Rh_{U,*}j_Y^{-1}e^{-1}A$ is an isomorphism. Clause (1) of [lem-kun-bc-base-change], applied to the original square followed by this open square, identifies the restricted $\beta_A$, followed by this isomorphism, with the exchange for $U$. The opens $X'_U$ cover $X'$. Every geometric point of $X'$ factors through one of them, so [lem-kun-stalk-faithful-derived] implies that it suffices to prove the assertion for every affine $U$. Fix one and rename it $Z=\operatorname{Spec}B$.

source.place: Tag 0F1I, lemma-punctual-base-change, first paragraph of proof; Tag 0EZT, lemma-base-change-Rf-star-colim, assertion (2)

proof.text: Let $I$ be the set of finitely generated $K$-subalgebras $B_i\subseteq B$, ordered by inclusion. By [lem-kun-algebra-union] this is a nonempty directed set and $B=\bigcup_i B_i$. More explicitly, the image of $K$ supplies an initial subalgebra, and the subalgebra generated by the union of two finite generating sets is an upper bound. This union is the ring colimit: compatible ring maps from the $B_i$ define a map on $B$ by sending an element using any subalgebra containing it; directedness makes this independent of the choice and ensures addition and multiplication are respected. Set $Z_i=\operatorname{Spec}B_i$. The finite generating set gives a one-affine-chart finite-type structure morphism $Z_i\to\operatorname{Spec}K$, by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism].

source.place: Tag 0F1I, lemma-punctual-base-change, first paragraph of proof; Tag 0EZT, lemma-base-change-Rf-star-colim, assertion (2)

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-colimit-limit], $Z=\varprojlim_i Z_i$ in schemes and the transition maps $Z_j\to Z_i$ are affine. Set $X'_i=Z_i\times_KS'$ and $Y_i=Z_i\times_KT$, with projections $f'_i:X'_i\to S'$, $h_i:Y_i\to X'_i$, and $e_i:Y_i\to T$. There is a cartesian square $(X'_i,Y_i,S',T)$ with bottom arrow $g$ for every $i$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-limit-fibre-products] to the systems $(Z_i,\operatorname{Spec}K,S')$ and $(Z_i,\operatorname{Spec}K,T)$, where the last two factors are constant systems. It gives affine transition maps on $X'_i$ and $Y_i$ and identifies their limits with $Z\times_KS'=X'$ and $Z\times_KT=Y$. The other two systems are constant with limits $S'$ and $T$ and identity (hence affine) transitions. These limits and identifications respect every projection by the fibre-product universal property. The upper-right scheme $Z\times_KT$ equals $X'\times_{S'}T$ through its two projections, so the limit square is precisely the original square.

source.place: Tag 0F1I, lemma-punctual-base-change, first paragraph of proof; Tag 0EZT, lemma-base-change-Rf-star-colim, assertion (2)

proof.text: For every $i$, apply [lem-kun-0f1i] with its finite-type $K$-scheme $X=Z_i$, the original $S'$, the original qcqs morphism $g:T\to S'$, and coefficient $A$. The finite-type hypothesis was checked in Step 3; Step 1 checked the invertible-order torsion condition on $A$. No finite-type hypothesis on $S'$ or $T$ is required by that node. It makes the canonical unbounded abelian exchange of [def-kun-unbounded-exchange] (at $\Lambda=\mathbf Z$, $A$ in degree zero) for the $i$-th square an isomorphism. By [lem-kun-unbounded-exchange-agrees] that map is the image under the inclusion $D^+\hookrightarrow D$ of the bounded-below exchange $(f'_i)^{-1}Rg_*A\to Rh_{i,*}e_i^{-1}A$ of [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange], under the canonical comparisons of its endpoints; as $D^+$ is a full subcategory [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories], this bounded-below exchange is an isomorphism. By [lem-kun-bc-map-on-cohomology], for every $q\ge0$ its cohomology map is the usual degree-$q$ base-change map, which is therefore an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0F1I, lemma-punctual-base-change, first paragraph of proof; Tag 0EZT, lemma-base-change-Rf-star-colim, assertion (2)

proof.text: Fix $q\ge0$. In [lem-kun-0ezt], use the inverse system of squares in Step 4, with its $(X_i,Y_i,S_i,T_i)=(X'_i,Y_i,S',T)$ and with $F_i=A$ and identity coefficient transitions on the constant $T$-system. The index set is directed by Step 3, all four transition morphisms are affine by Step 4, every $g_i=g$ is qcqs by hypothesis, and each $F_i$ is torsion by Step 1. Each projection $p_i:T\to T_i$ is the identity. Consequently $\varinjlim_i p_i^{-1}F_i=A$: a constant diagram with identity maps over a nonempty directed set has exactly the cocones given by one map from $A$. Step 5 supplies every degree-$q$ exchange hypothesis. The conclusion of [lem-kun-0ezt] is that the canonical degree-$q$ base-change map $(f')^{-1}R^qg_*A\to R^qh_*e^{-1}A$ for the original square is an isomorphism. This concerns the specified canonical maps, not merely isomorphisms of their endpoints.

source.place: Tag 0F1I, lemma-punctual-base-change, first paragraph of proof; Tag 0EZT, lemma-base-change-Rf-star-colim, assertion (2)

proof.text: Step 6 applies to each $q\ge0$. By [lem-kun-bc-map-on-cohomology], these are all nonnegative cohomology maps of $\beta_A$; the negative cohomology sheaves of both terms vanish, since $A$ is in degree zero and right-derived direct image and exact inverse image are left t-exact, as expressed by the injective-resolution computation of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] and [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-exact]. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology], applied in the full bounded-below subcategory, proves invertibility of $\beta_A$ for affine $Z$. Step 2 gives it for arbitrary $Z$, and [lem-weil-pbc-exchange-forget-coefficients] returns it to the exact $\mathbf F_\ell$-linear adjoint mate specified in the statement.

from.place: the arbitrary-scheme extension of the untensored base-change assertion, using affine finitely generated subalgebras and the 0EZT limit comparison

split_report.summary: Extended the existing finite-type-over-K abelian 0F1I theorem to arbitrary Z using affine opens, finitely generated K-subalgebras, Spec/limit and fibre-product continuity, and the existing 0EZT comparison. Explicitly checked coefficient forgetting, injective restriction and canonical exchange compatibility. No new nodes and no statement change. Corrected the source location: the affine approximation paragraph is in the proof of 0F1I, used by 0F1J. Maintainer reader (Q43 review): added the termwise-exchange citation in Step 2 and the unbounded/bounded-below exchange agreement in Step 5.
split_report.blueprint: lem-kun-0f1j.proof.md, last finite-pushforward paragraph: removes the unjustified assertion that every finite cover X_i of an arbitrary affine X is finite type over K, by proving the arbitrary-scheme untensored input via the first paragraph of Stacks 0F1I. This is the precise place recorded in blueprint.from.place.

tool_uses.why: Forgets constant module coefficients while identifying the canonical exchange; the unit has no coefficient-forgetting theorem.
Exactness of abelian inverse image, used to restrict resolutions and identify negative cohomology; generic site tool.
Restriction to an etale open preserves injective resolutions; generic site tool absent from this unit.
Identifies the canonical open-square exchange termwise; generic site localization tool.
Converts the subalgebra colimit to the inverse limit of affine schemes; a generic algebraic geometry tool.
Provides affine transitions and the two product-limit identifications needed to apply the unit's 0EZT theorem.
Detects isomorphisms by cohomology in the full bounded-below subcategory; generic derived-category tool.
Identifies the derived exchange of the open restriction square with the termwise underived exchange on an injective resolution; generic exchange tool, the unit has no such statement.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q43-114b5b0a5 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole item and all seven steps, every cited statement, and Stacks etale-cohomology.tex at lemma-punctual-base-change (0F1I) proof paragraph 1, lemma-base-change-Rf-star-colim (0EZT)(2) and the start of the 0F1J proof. The statement is 0F1I for an arbitrary K-scheme Z, specialised to F_ell coefficients with ell invertible in K, which is exactly how the parent lem-kun-0f1j uses it (its Step 4). The map is the F_ell-linear mate in D^+. Edge cases Z empty, F=0, Z=Spec K and B=K[t1,t2,...] are all consistent. The route follows 0F1I paragraph 1: reduce to affine Z, write it as a limit of finite-type Spec B_i, apply lem-kun-0f1i to each, then pass to the limit with lem-kun-0ezt. Every hypothesis holds: the index set is directed and nonempty, all transitions are affine, g is qcqs, and A is ell-torsion. There are no new nodes, no duplicate (I grepped 0F1I and punctual-base-change), no cycle and no SGA. I fixed two missing citations (C1/C3/C4). (1) Step 2 went from 'the termwise underived exchange is an isomorphism' to 'the derived open exchange is an isomorphism' without a cited statement. It now cites lem-weil-pbc-derived-exchange-termwise with J=j_Y^{-1}I, which is K-injective by lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative. The termwise lemma is declared as a tool use. (2) Step 5 treated lem-kun-0f1i's unbounded exchange (def-kun-unbounded-exchange) as the bounded-below exchange of def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange. It now cites lem-kun-unbounded-exchange-agrees and the fullness of D^+ in D (def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories). I accepted the declared tool_uses (coefficient forgetting, inverse-image exactness, injective restriction, underived open exchange, Spec/limit, product limits, cohomology criterion) plus the added termwise lemma. Statement unchanged.; 1 file(s) fixed by the reviewer
